subject: Default capture horizon and deletion paths — requests vs generated artifacts (Q&A)
messages:
From: Sofia Perez <sofia@cobaltan.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on default capture — prompts vs outputs

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot and need a clear, short explanation of what Redwood stores by default for: (1) raw requests/prompts, (2) model outputs/responses (including streaming), (3) derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks), and (4) transient state like KV cache.

Two follow-ups:
- Are prompts used for model improvements unless we opt out?
- If we request deletion via API or contract, what is the end-to-end timeline and audit evidence we get?

We sent an initial SOC2 questionnaire; I've attached the specific rows we're worried about. Can you confirm the default retention windows and provide the deletion workflow we can present to our security team?

Appreciate a brief one-page summary we can hand to compliance.

Best,
Sofia Perez
Head of Platform Security
Cobalt Analytics

Attachment: SOC2_evidence_request.xlsx (spreadsheet stub - rows referenced)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Perez <sofia@cobaltan.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture — prompts vs outputs

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. High level answer first, then a short table and next steps below.

TL;DR: By default Redwood captures request metadata and the request text (prompts) for a short retention window to support debugging/observability; model outputs (full responses) are retained longer to support billing, quality monitoring and customer playback. Derivatives (embeddings, reranks) are treated as artifacts with their own retention windows. KV cache is kept ephemeral and not persisted to long-term stores unless explicitly enabled.

Quick default windows (customer-hosted or default hosted plan unless overridden in contract):
- Prompts / raw request text: 14 days (default).
- Model outputs (responses, including streaming chunks): 90 days.
- Derivatives (embeddings, vectors, rerank indices): 180 days.
- Session/KV cache: Ephemeral — kept in memory for the session and flushed; not written to persistent storage by default.

Deletion workflow (summary):
1) Customer-initiated: support ticket or API delete request -> mark artifacts for soft-delete immediately.
2) Soft-delete window: 30 days (audit trail retained).
3) Final purge: permanent removal from primary stores and object storage after soft-delete completes.
4) Backups / cold archives: retained for up to 90 additional days and purged per backup policy (we provide purge confirmation).

We do not use customer prompts to train upstream models by default unless you opt into explicit data sharing/training programs (we add a contract clause and an opt-in flag).

I'll loop in Kimberly for the deletion evidence and talk through the erasure runbook. Attached is a short retention summary PDF and the runbook draft; happy to adapt to Cobalt's wording.

Next steps:
- Kimberly will confirm the erasure trail and the timeline for evidence.
- I can provide a one-page extract you can include in your procurement/IR pack.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: retention_process_diagram.png (diagram), erasure_runbook.docx (runbook stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Perez <sofia@cobaltan.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture — prompts vs outputs

Hi Sofia,

Quick technical clarifications from Security/Compliance side:
- Deletion traceability: when a delete is issued we log the request id, initiating user, timestamp, and artifact ids. That audit record remains immutable (append-only) and is stored separately from the deleted content to prove erasure.
- Soft-delete vs purge: soft-delete marks objects inaccessible; purge removes objects and updates ledger entries to show completion. You receive a signed purge confirmation (CSV) and an audit entry id you can reference.
- Backups: incremental backups are retained for disaster recovery up to 90 days after purge; as part of a compliance engagement we can provide evidence of a purge from backups on demand (this is a manual activity and we include the time-to-remediate in the contract).
- Key material & encryption: all persisted artifacts are encrypted with customer or platform keys depending on deployment (KMS options available for Private deployments).

Private deployment note: for Private / on-prem installs, retention defaults are the same but can be configured to your policy and you own the final purge path. We will still provide the erasure runbook and audit template to use locally.

I suggest the following customer-facing sentence for contracts: "Redwood retains customer requests (prompts) for 14 days and model outputs for 90 days by default. Customers may request immediate soft-delete via API or support ticket; permanent purge follows a 30-day safety window and documented confirmation is provided. Backups are retained up to 90 days after purge."

I will attach the erasure runbook and a short sample purge-confirmation CSV for your security team.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: erasure_runbook.docx (runbook), SOC2_evidence_request_response.csv (sample purge confirmation - generated)

From: Sofia Perez <sofia@cobaltan.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-11T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture — prompts vs outputs

Thanks Ben and Kim — this is helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we close:
1) Residency: if we select EU residency for the tenant, does the 14/90/180 policy still apply but scoped to EU storage? In other words, are prompts stored in-region by default?
2) Embeddings: you listed 180 days by default — is that to support similarity search caching only, or are embeddings used for any internal model tuning?
3) Private deployment: you noted defaults are configurable — how quickly can we change the prompt retention window (e.g., from 14 days -> 0 days) in a Private install?

Also can you confirm we get a signed purge-confirmation CSV and an audit entry id — we need that for our regulator.

If you can provide a single-page summary and a short contract clause we can insert (one sentence + timeline), we can move to procurement.

Best,
Sofia

P.S. Jared from our infra team will join the next call to review residency mapping.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Perez <sofia@cobaltan.com>, Jared Liu <jared.liu@cobaltan.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture — prompts vs outputs

Hi Sofia / Jared — quick answers to your clarifying points and action items below.

1) Residency: yes. If you choose EU residency, all persisted artifacts (prompts, outputs, derivatives) are stored in-region by default. The retention windows above still apply unless you request a contractual change. EU residency also means backup geo-scope is limited to EU regions.

2) Embeddings usage: embeddings retained by default (180 days) are used only for operations you control (search, rerank) and for platform-level caching/efficiency. Embeddings are not used to train or fine-tune Redwood models on your behalf unless you explicitly opt in to a training program.

3) Private deployment retention change velocity: on Private installs, retention is a configuration toggle; changes can be applied by your infra team and take effect immediately for new data. Pre-existing artifacts follow the configured migration policy (we provide a one-time migration/purge job which typically completes within 24–72 hours depending on dataset size).

Evidence and contract language: we will provide:
- Signed purge-confirmation CSV with artifact ids and timestamps.
- Immutable audit entry id for each delete operation.
- Proposed contract sentence (for insertion): "Redwood will retain prompts for 14 days and outputs for 90 days by default; upon customer request Redwood will initiate a soft-delete and provide a signed purge confirmation within 30 days of request completion."

Action items: 
- Ben: produce a one-page summary tailored for procurement (linked).
- Kim: attach the sample purge CSV and the erasure runbook (done).
- Redwood to add residency confirmation clause to the SOW for the pilot.

I'll upload the one-pager to the shared Drive link and drop the HubSpot note on DEAL-8742. Let me know if you want this language made more prescriptive for legal review.

Thanks,
